import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Two field settings keep sensitive values out of sight, and they solve two
different problems. A `secret` field stores a credential in an encrypted
store beside the document; the document carries only a marker. A `write_only`
field accepts a value, hands it to the script, and then throws it away.

## When to use this

Use a `secret` field for a value the system must keep: an API key, a password
hash, a one-time token. Use a `write_only` field for a value the script needs
once and nobody should keep, such as a plaintext password that the script
hashes.

| | `secret` field | `write_only` field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Value kept | Yes, encrypted, outside documents | No, discarded after the write |
| Visible on read | No, a marker only | No, gone after the write |
| Visible in history, search, exports | No | No |
| Visible to scripts | No, only the marker | Yes, during the write |
| Change and clear | Yes, from the document page | Not applicable |

## Before you start

- **A draft domain.** You edit the doctype in a [draft domain](/build/model/in-app/how-drafts-work/), or in the
  [domain folder on a dev server](/build/model/in-files/domain-files/).
- **A mode.** A `secret` field declares a `mode`: `hash` for values that are
  only ever checked, `sealed` for values the system must read back itself,
  and `token` for a one-time value Facet generates.
- **The limits.** Secrets never appear in actions as arguments, in arrays or
  dictionaries, or in the display name and search templates. Facet refuses
  the definition otherwise.

## Steps

<Tabs syncKey="build-mode">
<TabItem label="Builder">

1. Open the doctype in the **Builder** and add a field.
2. Pick the type **Secret** and choose the mode: **Hash**, **Sealed**, or
   **Token**. A token asks for its lifetime in seconds.
3. For a write-only input, add a text field and tick **Write only**.

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Files">

```yaml
# a service doctype in your domain (extract)
fields:
  api_key:
    type: secret
    mode: sealed
    title: API key
  reset_code:
    type: secret
    mode: token
    ttl_seconds: 3600
  new_password:
    type: string
    write_only: true
    title: New password
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

### Rules per mode

| Mode | Use | Extra key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hash` | Verify a candidate against the stored value, never read it back. | — |
| `sealed` | The system reads the value back for its own features. | — |
| `token` | Facet generates the value; a caller consumes it once. | `ttl_seconds` (required, a positive number of seconds) |

`min`, `max`, and `pattern` are allowed on a secret field; they check the
plaintext when it is set, not the marker.

### Set the value in the app

The document page shows a marker with **Change** and **Clear**. A change
stages the new value: Facet stores it and bumps the version on the marker. A
`token` mode shows **Generate new** and displays the token once.

### How a write-only field works

The script of the doctype reads the value during the write, does its work,
and Facet strips the field before the document is stored. The common pairing
is a `read_only` hash field: the script hashes the write-only input and
stores the hash there, because a `secret` field accepts only staged values.

## Example

A small service registry inside a Brightwater-style operations domain:

```json
{
  "domain": "ops",
  "doctype": "Service",
  "aggregate_root": true,
  "schema_version": 1,
  "fields": {
    "name": { "type": "string", "required": true, "filters": ["equality", "text_search"] },
    "api_key": { "type": "secret", "mode": "sealed" },
    "reset_code": { "type": "secret", "mode": "token", "ttl_seconds": 3600 },
    "new_password": { "type": "string", "write_only": true }
  }
}
```

A stored document carries markers instead of values:

```json
{
  "name": "Billing",
  "api_key": { "mode": "sealed", "version": 3, "set_at": "2026-03-01T09:12:00Z" }
}
```

A cleared secret stores `null`. A `write_only` field never appears in stored
content at all.

## Troubleshooting

### The write answers `422` on the secret field

Only three shapes are valid: a stage handle, a marker, and `null` to clear. A
plaintext string in a document body is always rejected.

### The token was shown once and is lost

Tokens display once, at generation. Generate a new one; the old token stops
working.

### An admin cannot read the value back

That is the design. No route returns a sealed or hashed value. Only the
system features that own the field read it, and a hashed value is never
readable at all. To rotate, set a new value; the marker version rises.

The values sit in the encrypted store, keyed by document and field name,
outside the document tables. When a document is deleted, the store keeps its
slots until the retention window passes; a maintenance task then removes
them.

### The write-only value is needed again later

It is gone. Facet never stores it. Keep the source of the value outside Facet
if you need it again.

:::caution
Rolling a document back to an earlier state does not restore old secret
values. The current values stay in place, and old credentials never come
back.
:::
